SOLACE

Chapter One Edition

  • Rotate your phone to landscape.
  • Touch the left side of the screen to walk.
  • Action adapts to your target: chop, mine, pick, attack, drink.
  • Water: sea water gives little and can make you sick. Build a Rain Collector (Carpenter) for clean water, carry a Waterskin (Leather from cows, deer, boars and goats), and boil bucket water at a Campfire.
  • Defense: the Cannon post (Salvage Bench) fires at hostile enemies in range. Press Action on it to load Cannonballs.
  • Fill the 5 hotbar slots from your Bag. Items moved to the hotbar (and armor you wear) leave the Bag and no longer use Bag slots. Tap a slot to equip it, tap again to eat or place. The Bag holds 15 kinds of items, 20 of each. Store the rest in a Chest (30 slots, 20 of each item per slot), including spare tools and armor.
  • Craft a Workbench or Carpenter table first (Bag → Craft). Tools, buildings and gear are made at tables: walk up to a Workbench, Carpenter, Anvil, Mason, Furnace or Oven and press Action to open it. Cook at a Campfire. Chests within 3 tiles of a table or campfire count as materials too, so you don't have to take items out first (tools and armor are not pulled from chests). Every craft takes a few seconds; progress shows inside the crafting menu. Repairing buildings needs a Hammer. Tools wear out and break.
  • You can swim: an energy bar appears and drains (about 10 tiles of water). When it runs out you drown: you wake up at your last bed (or on the first island) and lose 30% of the materials in your bag. Tools and armor are safe. You cannot act while swimming. Dashing while in the water costs an extra 10% of swim energy.
  • Craft a hoe, equip it, till grass, plant seeds, water, harvest.
  • Wolves come at night. Build walls and a door.
  • Sheep drop wool for beds and fishing lines. Fish: cast, tap on a bite, then hold Action to keep the green zone on the fish.
  • The Forgotten Seas. There was once an age when the seas belonged to kings. Great fleets sailed beneath golden banners, merchants traveled between distant kingdoms, and the bells of coastal cities echoed across the waters. But no age of prosperity lasts forever. Wars consumed the great kingdoms. Famine swept across the countryside, and ancient cities were abandoned as their rulers fought over what little remained. The old trade routes fell silent. Those who survived fled toward the distant islands, seeking lands untouched by war and hunger. Some established villages. Others built fortresses and declared themselves kings. And some were never heard from again. As centuries passed, the seas became a place of forgotten histories. Sailors spoke of islands where the dead still wandered, forests where daylight never reached the ground, and ancient ruins that appeared on no known map. Yet not every island was cursed. Life continued. Fishermen cast their nets, blacksmiths worked their forges, and travelers still crossed the waters in search of fortune. For the world had not ended. It had merely grown darker. And somewhere among these countless islands, the remains of the old world still waited to be discovered. Elves and dwarves do not like each other.
  • Villages (🏘️ and ⚓ islands) have houses with beds and chests, farms and villagers. Face a villager and tap Action to talk. Each villager trades according to their job: merchants, farmers, fishermen, elders and strangers all want different goods. Harbors add their own trades: the harbormaster, dockhand, fishmonger, shipwright, lighthouse keeper and sailor. The village guards (4 Spearmen and 2 Archers in both villages and harbors) do not trade: they chase down and kill any monster they see.
  • Tame animals: hold a plant or fruit they like and tap Action. Watch the thought bubble to see what they want. Build a Fence pen, then shear wool and take eggs.
  • Two tamed animals of the same kind breed when both are full and close together (max 2 babies each). Hold a sword to attack tamed animals.
